$comment: The launchd jobs bin/gen-launchd renders to scheduled/*.plist.tmpl. Edit this file,
then run bin/gen-launchd. The schema is at the top of bin/gen-launchd-lib.js.

jobs.label: com.danielhunter.pr-dash
why: Definition only — this file is outside `home/`, so chezmoi never deploys it.
Kept out of the source root for a reason specific to launchd: it reads a plist only at
bootstrap, so an auto-deployed copy means `chezmoi apply` rewrites the file while the
loaded job keeps the old definition. A port or a path change then looks applied and is
not. Rendering by hand makes re-activation an explicit step instead of a skipped one.
A TEMPLATE, so activation renders it rather than symlinking it. launchd expands nothing
in a plist — not $HOME, not ~ — and both ProgramArguments and StandardOutPath have to be
absolute, so a hardcoded /Users/daniel would work on one machine under one account.
Activate on a machine that wants the dashboard always listening on 127.0.0.1:8770:
mkdir -p -m 700 ~/.local/state/pr-dash
chezmoi execute-template \
< ~/.local/share/chezmoi/scheduled/com.danielhunter.pr-dash.plist.tmpl \
> ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.danielhunter.pr-dash.plist
launchctl bootstrap "gui/$(id -u)" ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.danielhunter.pr-dash.plist
The mkdir is not optional: launchd creates the log file but not its parent, and the
payload store only creates that directory after the process has already spawned. Mode
700 matches DIR_MODE in src/payload-store.ts — the directory holds private PR titles,
and this host's `umask 0007` would otherwise leave it group-writable.
Deactivate:
launchctl bootout "gui/$(id -u)/com.danielhunter.pr-dash"
rm ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.danielhunter.pr-dash.plist
What that costs: the bookmark stops working, since nothing holds the port any more.
`pr-dash` in a terminal still starts a server and opens the browser on it.
Reload after editing this file. launchd read the old definition at bootstrap and will
keep serving it until the job is replaced, so this is the step whose absence makes an
edit look applied when it is not:
launchctl bootout "gui/$(id -u)/com.danielhunter.pr-dash"
chezmoi execute-template \
< ~/.local/share/chezmoi/scheduled/com.danielhunter.pr-dash.plist.tmpl \
> ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.danielhunter.pr-dash.plist
launchctl bootstrap "gui/$(id -u)" ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.danielhunter.pr-dash.plist
Check it:
launchctl print "gui/$(id -u)/com.danielhunter.pr-dash"
tail -f ~/.local/state/pr-dash/agent.log
The same reload block is what a code change needs. `chezmoi apply` deploys new `public/`
assets under the running server, which serves them per request, while `src/` stays at
whatever the process loaded — so a change to the /api/prs response shape leaves a new
app.js validating an old server's body. That is a 60-second poll and a give-up banner
for up to the 16-hour idle window, which daily use may never reach, so reloading the job
is the fix rather than waiting it out.

ProgramArguments: Reached through fnm's aliases/default symlink, not a version-pinned path, so an
fnm upgrade does not silently strand this agent on a removed Node version.
env.PR_DASH_WORK_ORGS: The GitHub owners whose repositories the dashboard shows by default; everything
else is hidden until the Personal chip is on. Comma-separated, and the name
itself stays out of this repo, which is public-posture: it comes from
[data]. Rendering on a machine that sets no such key emits an empty string,
which src/main-lib.ts's parseWorkOrgs reads as no work organizations at all —
every repository then counts as work and the chip stays hidden.
env.PR_DASH_EXTENSION_ORIGINS: The Chrome extension origins allowed to read the routes in src/server.ts's EXTENSION_PATHS cross-origin,
comma-separated, each chrome-extension://<32-letter id>. The ID stays out of this repo: it comes
from `prDashExtensionOrigins` in the machine-local chezmoi.toml, under [data].
Unset renders an empty string, which accepts no extension origin, and a malformed
entry makes src/main.ts exit at startup rather than serve a wider boundary than
configured. launchd reads this only at bootstrap, so a changed key needs the
reload block in this file's header, not just `chezmoi apply`.
env.PR_DASH_VULN_REPOS: The repositories the vulnerabilities page (/vulns.html) lists open Dependabot alerts
for and the repositories page (/repos.html) summarizes, comma-separated owner/name.
The names stay out of this repo: they come from
`prDashVulnRepos` in the machine-local chezmoi.toml, under [data]. Unset renders an
empty string, and the page then says no repositories are configured. A malformed
entry makes src/main.ts exit at startup rather than silently drop a repository.
The token needs Dependabot-alert read access on each one, or that repository shows
env.PATH: src/token.ts invokes `op` by bare name through execFile, and launchd's default
PATH is just /usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin. Without /opt/homebrew/bin here, the
first /api/prs comes back as a 500 carrying an ENOENT.
KeepAlive: Bare <true/>, never a dict with SuccessfulExit <false/>. The idle exit (main-lib.ts's
createIdleExit) exits status 0 by design. Under SuccessfulExit: false, launchd reads
a clean exit as "do not restart", so the port would go dead until the next login and
nothing in this suite would notice.
ThrottleInterval: launchd's own default, named explicitly so the dependency is visible rather than
inherited. It bounds how long the port sits unheld after an idle exit.

jobs.label: com.daniel.retention-sweep
why: The macOS half of the hourly retention sweep. Linux runs it as
home/dot_config/systemd/user/retention-sweep.{service,timer}; this is the same job, with
the same one argument, which tells the sweeper to act. It is the only thing that prunes
~/.claude/artifacts here: manifest rows G20 and G21 replaced the SessionStart hook
prune-artifacts.sh.
Acting covers every APPLY_ROWS row, not only the artifact rows. That includes G14 and
G15, which prune known /tmp prefixes older than a day.
Definition only. Like its siblings it lives outside `home/`, so chezmoi never deploys it
and the job runs only on a machine that activates it by hand.
The label is com.daniel.retention-sweep, outside com.daniel.claude.*, because
work-laptop-config's catch-up.sh globs that prefix and runs `eval` on
ProgramArguments.2. Here that element is the sweeper's path, so a replay would run the
sweep outside its launcher. RunAtLoad covers a missed hour instead.
Activate:
chezmoi execute-template \
< ~/.local/share/chezmoi/scheduled/com.daniel.retention-sweep.plist.tmpl \
> ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.daniel.retention-sweep.plist
launchctl bootstrap "gui/$(id -u)" \
~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.daniel.retention-sweep.plist
Deactivate:
launchctl bootout "gui/$(id -u)/com.daniel.retention-sweep"
rm ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.daniel.retention-sweep.plist
Check it: the last line of the log reports what the last run pruned, and
~/.claude/.retention-sweep-last-run holds the same counts as JSON.

ProgramArguments: Started through run-python.sh, under the uv-managed Python 3.15 the hooks use.
The sweeper's own #!/usr/bin/env python3 resolves to Apple's /usr/bin/python3 on
launchd's PATH, which is 3.9 and lacks os.path.realpath(strict=), so every
env.PATH: Puts uv on PATH for run-python.sh's interpreter lookup. When that lookup fails it
falls back to python3, which this PATH resolves to Homebrew's rather than 3.9.
StartInterval: Hourly, as the systemd timer's OnCalendar=hourly. RunAtLoad stands in for its
Persistent=true: launchd has no catch-up for a machine that was asleep.

jobs.label: com.daniel.transcript-scan
why: The macOS half of the daily transcript credential sweep. Linux runs it as
home/dot_config/systemd/user/claude-transcript-scan.{service,timer}; this is the same job.
Why it needs to exist separately from the SessionEnd hook. The hook
(home/private_dot_claude/hooks/executable_session-end.sh) already scans each transcript as
its session ends, on every platform, and that is the normal path. The timer exists for the
sessions where the hook never completed — a kill -9, a crash, or a scan that outlived its
parent. On macOS that catch-up did not exist at all: ten systemd timers on Linux against
two plists here, and this was the one whose absence had teeth.
A TEMPLATE, like its siblings: launchd expands neither $HOME nor ~ in a plist, and
StandardOutPath must be absolute. Rendering costs the symlink — the copy in
~/Library/LaunchAgents stops tracking edits here, so a change means re-running Activate.
Definition only. Like its siblings it lives outside `home/`, so chezmoi never deploys it
and the job runs only on a machine that activates it by hand.
The label is com.daniel.transcript-scan, outside com.daniel.claude.*, because
work-laptop-config's catch-up.sh globs that prefix in ~/Library/LaunchAgents.
catch-up.sh replays a missed job by running `eval` on ProgramArguments.2, a convention only
run-skill.sh plists follow. Here that element is "25", the scan window in hours, so every pass
after 07:00 would run `eval 25`, exit 127, and never write the .done marker that stops it.
The job handles its own missed runs through RunAtLoad, described below.
Activate:
chezmoi execute-template \
< ~/.local/share/chezmoi/scheduled/com.daniel.transcript-scan.plist.tmpl \
> ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.daniel.transcript-scan.plist
launchctl bootstrap "gui/$(id -u)" \
~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.daniel.transcript-scan.plist
Deactivate:
launchctl bootout "gui/$(id -u)/com.daniel.transcript-scan"
rm ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.daniel.transcript-scan.plist
The 25-hour window below matches the unit: a day's window with an hour of overlap, because
it has to cover more than the interval between runs, or a slow day loses transcripts.
RunAtLoad is true where the systemd timer instead sets Persistent=true. They answer the
same question — a machine that was asleep at the scheduled hour must still sweep — but
launchd has no Persistent, and its own catch-up for a missed StartCalendarInterval fires
only once on wake and is not something to rely on for a security control.
Exit 1 (findings) and exit 3 (could-not-evaluate) both matter here, and launchd reports
neither. That is why the scanner writes ~/.claude/logs/transcript-leaks-pending and
the Claude Code statusline shows it until it is cleared: on this platform the plist's log
file is the only other trace, and nobody reads a log file unprompted.

jobs.label: com.daniel.claude.changelog-watch
why: Definition only — this file is outside `home/`, so chezmoi never deploys it.
Kept out of the source root on purpose: it must NOT land in ~/Library/LaunchAgents,
because work-laptop-config's catch-up.sh globs that directory and would replay the
job even while it is unloaded.
A TEMPLATE, so activation renders it rather than symlinking it. launchd expands nothing
in a plist — not $HOME, not ~ — and StandardOutPath in particular has to be an absolute
path, so the home directory was written out as /Users/daniel and the file only worked on
one machine under one account. That is the same defect tests/scheduled-tasks.test.js was
written to catch in the Windows Task Scheduler exports; it was fixed there and left here.
Rendering costs the symlink: the copy in ~/Library/LaunchAgents no longer tracks edits to
this file, so changing the schedule means re-running the activate block below.
Activate on a machine that wants the daily /changelog-watch run:
chezmoi execute-template \
< ~/.local/share/chezmoi/scheduled/com.daniel.claude.changelog-watch.plist.tmpl \
> ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.daniel.claude.changelog-watch.plist
launchctl bootstrap "gui/$(id -u)" \
~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.daniel.claude.changelog-watch.plist
Deactivate:
launchctl bootout "gui/$(id -u)/com.daniel.claude.changelog-watch"
rm ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.daniel.claude.changelog-watch.plist
The `/changelog-watch` command itself lives in this repo at
home/private_dot_claude/commands/changelog-watch.md and stays available to run by
hand regardless of whether this agent is loaded.
Linux boxes schedule the same job through systemd instead, and need no manual
activation — the units deploy with chezmoi and a run_onchange script enables the
timer:
home/dot_config/systemd/user/claude-changelog-watch.{service,timer}
home/dot_local/bin/executable_claude-changelog-watch   (runner; no run-skill.sh)
Runner dependency: run-skill.sh is provided by the work-laptop-config repo
(symlinked to ~/.claude/scheduled/run-skill.sh), so activation needs that repo
installed. It runs the skill headless with permission prompts disabled (the
dangerously-skip-permissions flag) and
renders an HTML artifact in `shown` mode.

jobs.label: com.daniel.claude-otel
why: Not active on any machine. The work Mac (MacBook-Pro-2) was its only user, and its stack
was removed on 2026-10-20: the org's managed settings send that machine's telemetry to
Lithic's collector, so a local stack receives nothing. .chezmoiignore no longer deploys
~/claude-otel there. Kept as the definition for a Mac that runs its own collector.
Definition only. This file is outside `home/`, so chezmoi never deploys it. launchd reads
a plist only at bootstrap, so an auto-deployed copy would let `chezmoi apply` rewrite the
file while the loaded job kept the old definition. The script it runs,
~/claude-otel/ensure-up.sh, IS deployed by chezmoi (home/claude-otel/executable_ensure-up.sh,
darwin only).
What it does: on a Mac running Docker Desktop, runs ensure-up.sh at load and whenever
~/.docker/run/docker.sock changes, which is how Docker Desktop starting announces itself.
The script waits for `docker info` to answer, then runs `docker compose up -d` on
~/claude-otel. See home/claude-otel/README.md for the stack itself.
A TEMPLATE, so activation renders it rather than symlinking it. launchd expands neither
$HOME nor ~ anywhere in a plist, and ProgramArguments, WatchPaths and the log paths all
have to be absolute.
Activate:
chezmoi execute-template \
< ~/.local/share/chezmoi/scheduled/com.daniel.claude-otel.plist.tmpl \
> ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.daniel.claude-otel.plist
launchctl bootstrap "gui/$(id -u)" ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.daniel.claude-otel.plist
Deactivate:
launchctl bootout "gui/$(id -u)/com.daniel.claude-otel"
rm ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.daniel.claude-otel.plist
The stack keeps running after a deactivate. Only the restart after Docker Desktop
restarts is lost; `docker compose -f ~/claude-otel/docker-compose.yml up -d` by hand still
works.
Reload after editing THIS file (bootout, re-render, bootstrap):
launchctl bootout "gui/$(id -u)/com.daniel.claude-otel"
chezmoi execute-template \
< ~/.local/share/chezmoi/scheduled/com.daniel.claude-otel.plist.tmpl \
> ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.daniel.claude-otel.plist
launchctl bootstrap "gui/$(id -u)" ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.daniel.claude-otel.plist
After editing only ensure-up.sh, `chezmoi apply ~/claude-otel` and then restart the job.
A running job keeps executing the script it started with:
launchctl kickstart -k "gui/$(id -u)/com.daniel.claude-otel"
Check it:
launchctl print "gui/$(id -u)/com.daniel.claude-otel"
tail ~/claude-otel/launchd.log
The label is com.daniel.claude-otel with a hyphen, not com.daniel.claude.otel. The
catch-up agent in work-laptop-config replays every com.daniel.claude.*.plist it finds in
~/Library/LaunchAgents, and this job has no schedule for it to replay.
